[RCTS.1.2.19] **`field_order`: a recording's fields in the order its
writer must write them.** A fixture whose `expect.kind` is `field_order`
carries two more fields: `steps`, the session's inputs as [RCTS.1.2.28] states
them; and `atoms`, a list of names of messages the `Atom` oneof holds. A
harness must fail the fixture when its recording holds no atom of a name
`atoms` lists, so that each is shown to be walked. A harness must record the session with the runtime's own recorder and
walk the recording from its `Stream` message by the field types `proto/`
declares: each length-delimited field whose type is a message is walked as
that message, and each fact body (`FactAssert.fact`, `FactEmit.fact`) is
walked as a message of one scalar field per slot ([RDSC.5.8.3]). The runtime
passes only when, in every message the walk reaches, each field's number is
at least the number of the field before it, and a field that is not repeated
appears at most once ([RFCS.19.5]).

Before it judges the recording, a harness must alter a copy of it: in the
first atom body whose first two fields have different numbers, those two
fields swap places, which keeps every length. A harness must fail the fixture
when its walk does not refuse that copy, or when no atom body has two such
fields.

A fixture whose `expect.kind` is `dsc_field_order` binds the other container
([RFCS.19.1]) and the compiler: it carries `atoms` and no `steps`. A harness
must compile `rules_ds` with the compiler under test and judge the `.dsc` it
writes as this clause judges a recording, walked from its `Dsc` message in
place of `Stream`, and with the same altered copy refused first. The compiler
passes only when every message the walk reaches keeps both rules above.
